title: Single-neuron encoding of rapidly learned visual information reshapes human perception
title_zh: 单个神经元对快速学习的视觉信息编码重塑人类感知
abstract: Humans can swiftly learn to recognize visual objects after minimal exposure. Integrating new information with existing knowledge requires forming enduring neuronal representations to enable future recognition. Yet, the neuronal mechanisms in the human brain underlying such rapid perceptual changes remain unclear. Here we recorded single-neuron activity in occipital cortex (OC) and medial temporal lobe (MTL) regions as participants rapidly learned to recognize degraded images. OC and MTL neurons modulated their activity to encode newly learned visual information and reshape perception. Population decoding revealed that OC neurons required additional processing time to resolve the identity of learned images, with delayed neuronal responses in the MTL. Our findings suggest that OC supports recognition after rapid learning via extensive recurrent processing, potentially involving higher-order neocortical areas, without relying on feedback from MTL. These results provide mechanistic constraints for biologically plausible models of visual recognition and few-shot visual learning. The authors show that rapid learning modulates neuronal activity in the human visual cortex, requiring extra processing time to support recognition and relaying signals to memory-related regions without requiring feedback.
abstract_zh: 人类在极少暴露后即可快速学会识别视觉对象。将新信息与现有知识整合需要形成持久的神经表征，以便实现未来的识别。然而，人类大脑中此类快速感知变化的神经机制仍不清楚。在此，我们在参与者快速学会识别模糊图像时，记录了视觉皮层（OC）和颞叶（MTL）区域的单个神经元活动。OC和MTL神经元调节其活动以编码新学习的视觉信息并重塑感知。人口解码揭示，OC神经元需要额外的处理时间来解析已学习图像的身份，MTL中神经反应延迟。我们的发现表明，OC通过广泛的反复处理在快速学习后支持识别，这可能涉及高阶新皮层区域，而无需依赖MTL的反馈。这些结果为视觉识别和少样本视觉学习的生物学合理模型提供了机制约束。作者表明，快速学习调节人类视觉皮层的神经活动，需要额外的处理时间来支持识别，并将信号传递到与记忆相关的区域，而无需依赖MTL反馈。
